rule.orchestrator: decides routing, admission, deferral, rate or cadence, recall placement or session retention, all enactable through the vLLM OpenAI API and the existing host tier
rule.engine: the mechanism lives inside the serving engine: scheduler internals, KV layout, or its own cache layer

arms.reason: it decides routing only: every episodic call and every recall stays on the device, so the orchestrator simply sends nothing to the server. It is the floor of the live comparison.

AttentionStore IS a host-side KV cache hierarchy with its own lookup, placement and prefetch inside the engine. An orchestrator can move a SESSION between tiers but cannot implement a cache layer under vLLM's attention, so what would run live is not AttentionStore.

LMCache is a CPU / disk KV cache layer under the engine. vLLM 0.31.0's native OffloadingConnector (`--kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 256`, the KV-HOST configuration this suite already measures) is the same kind of thing, so live it is represented by that SERVER CONFIGURATION and never by a policy. Any claim is about vLLM's native offload, not about LMCache.

its mechanism is MULTI-TIER PARTIAL RESIDENCY inside the KV manager - part of a session's cache resident, part not. The API exposes no partial residency, so only whole-session placement could be enacted, which is the mechanism removed rather than adapted.
which sessions are kept warm, from demand. Keeping a session warm is an orchestrator action (hold it on the GPU, push it to the host tier, or drop it).
